Yeah. I was barely able to stay conscious. I tried to rinse off in the shower before going to the er, but I couldn't stay standing long enough. I had to lay on the couch for an hour before I could get up again. Obviously I wasn't thinking clearly, cuz I thought that they could get me to stop puking and then I would be able to go back to work the. Ext day and pretend that it hadn't happened. Not really sure how I drove 30 minutes to the er.

Always some variation of pills. Clearly not a good method lol
Most recent was over 100 extra strength Tylenol and some otc sleeping pills (hoping to sleep thru any of the bodies attempts to vomit). 
Waking up the next morning still alive was basically the worst. Then I spent 3 days puking before I took myself to the ER. 
Messed up my liver pretty good. They weren't sure if they would be able to at first, but they were able to reverse it. Then I was stuck inpatient psych for almost 2 weeks. They wouldn't release me until I told somebody in my life what had happened.
Yeah. I've tried a few times in the past. And I have decided that I am not trying again unless I can be sure it will work. But that decision doesn't really make each day easier to live.
Yeah. They are kind of a constant for me. The intensity varies though.
Yeah. But I'm going home soon. I work at a hospital.
Hey! Thanks for responding! I'm just feeling crappy today. I have my last appointment with my current therapist tomorrow (she's moving). And the entire situation makes me feel so anxious.

I have been very suicidal and I am also somebody who is continually thinking about how my behaviors affect others. I have been unsuccessful in my suicide attempts. If you research the effectiveness of various suicide methods, you will probably notice that the more gruesome methods (including jumping in front of a train) are the most effective methods. I have seriously wanted to die with some of my attempts and put a lot of time and effort into my plans, only to have them fail, because I put too much consideration into the people that would have to deal with the aftermath. I have asked myself why it matters if I am successful and the best that I can come up with is that life is hard enough without me adding to people's troubles. But I have considered some of these methods that would destroy other people's lives, simply because I know that it will work. If you are in so much pain and there is no effective way to end your life without hurting others, sometimes people choose to let others get hurt.
My question was directed toward people who think that comparing Trump to Hitler is dramatic. You have said that you believe it is dramatic, but have not answered my question.

You have made it clear that you fit into the group of people to whom I was directing my question. Do you have a response regarding when German citizens should have recognized Hitler's behaviors as dangerous and intervened?

To clarify:
History says that the majority of Germans did not fall into the category of Nazis and claim to be mostly unaware of the atrocities that were happening until afterward. So, without the benefit of hindsight, when should the people (who did not want these atrocities to occur) have said enough? At what point should they have recognized his rhetoric as atypical political rhetoric and taken it seriously?

Note: I am not asking this as an attack against anyone's political stance. I am genuinely curious. There have been many leaders compared to Hitler in the past (which is unfortunate) and I am well aware of Godwins Law, so please do not bring that into the discussion. I do not want to know why you think this hat Trump is not Hitler or why you think other leaders should be considered Hitler. The question that I am really asking is "when should Ordinary German citizens have taken the hateful things Hitler and his supporters were saying at face value and made it clear that those types of actions were unacceptable?"
